requirements.text: The guards in scripts/kit.py are proven by tests, so the product is not trusted on faith
OpenCode users get the same tool-call blocking as Claude Code and Cursor users
Every pull request shows the kit's evidence result, so teams see proof without opening a terminal
Codex users install the guard hook with one command instead of manual steps

features.title: Test suite for the guards in scripts/kit.py

acceptance.check: A test creates a scratch git repo, runs kit.py init, and kit.py check exits 0
Editing scripts/kit.py in a scratch repo makes kit.py check exit non-zero with 'protected guard file changed'
kit.py done fails when any acceptance criterion of the feature has no PASS evidence
Deleting or skipping an existing test (for example adding .skip) is reported by kit.py check
dep-check or check reports a new package that has no entry in docs/dependencies.md

features.notes: New test files only, under tests/. Do not edit scripts/kit.py to make tests pass. If a test exposes a real bug, record it in agent/known-issues.md and ask the human for GUARD_ADMIN=1.

features.title: OpenCode guard plugin

acceptance.check: An OpenCode plugin file in .opencode/plugins/ loads without error in OpenCode
The plugin's tool.execute.before hook throws when the tool call edits a protected guard file
The plugin lets ordinary edits through without throwing

features.notes: Guard files are human-only: a human must set GUARD_ADMIN=1 to commit the plugin. Verify the exact tool.execute.before signature in https://opencode.ai/docs/plugins/ first and record it in docs/decisions.md. Hook behaviour is verified only by running OpenCode, not by reading the docs.

features.title: Pull request comment with the kit's evidence result

acceptance.check: On a pull request, the CI workflow posts one comment with the verify summary (PASS, FAIL or SKIP per gate)
When the kit check fails, the workflow fails and the comment names the failing gate
The comment step runs only with pull-requests: write permission and never prints secrets

features.notes: .github/workflows/verify.yml is a CI file and may be protected: treat changes as human-approved. Update the comment in place on re-runs instead of posting a new one each time.

features.title: One-command Codex guard hook installer

acceptance.check: kit.py hooks --install writes ~/.codex/config.toml and ~/.codex/hooks.json with the guard entry
Running the installer twice does not duplicate the hook entry
An existing ~/.codex/hooks.json with other hooks is merged, not overwritten

features.notes: Writes to the user's home folder. Show the diff and ask before writing. kit.py is protected: a human sets GUARD_ADMIN=1 to commit the change.
